Position Details Position Information Winthrop Position Title Adjunct - CAS Job Description The College of Arts and Sciences at Winthrop University seeks dynamic and qualified Adjunct Faculty to teach in disciplines across its 12 academic departments. The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to high-quality, student-centered instruction that is informed by strong academic credentials and real-world experiences. Applicants should be passionate about fostering student success in an engaging learning environment. Position Responsibilities Adjunct faculty, part-time appointments, are expected to adhere to all policies and procedures expected of university employees. Adjunct faculty will: Offer evidence of effective Student Intellectual Development activities Demonstrate a commitment to meeting the academic responsibility requirements for all faculty (e.g., adherence to academic policies, participating in the collection of assessment data necessary for course and program evaluation). Attend any College orientation sessions. Develop and distribute a written course syllabus as outlined by university policy and College policy at the first course meeting. Present course content as announced to students and as approved by the faculty. Meet all assigned classes or make appropriate alternative arrangements for the class when an absence is unavoidable. Schedule and maintain regular office hours (in-person or virtual) and be available to students. Award academic credit based on the professional evaluation of academic performance. Observe the policies and procedures of the department, College, and the University. Administer student evaluations and any additional assessment instruments required by the University. File an annual report that provides evidence of progress and involvement that is responsive to feedback and meets expectations of rank. In its colleges of Arts and Sciences; Business and Technology; Education, Sport, and Human Sciences; and Visual and Performing Arts, Winthrop embraces only those programs and activities that can be delivered at an exemplary level. Winthrop University is achieving national stature as a competitive and distinctive co-educational, public, residential, comprehensive, values-oriented institution. The values of service, excellence, community, and leadership provide the foundation for Winthrop’s continuing development and shape Winthrop’s continuing success. Numerous national accolades reflect the sustained high quality and value of the Winthrop Experience, including the most recent U.S. News & World Report’s ranking of Winthrop as one of the top-10 public comprehensive universities in the South. Winthrop is an active member of the Rock Hill community and recognized as a key component of the region’s economic resurgence. Approximately 20 minutes from Charlotte, North Carolina, Winthrop has direct access to and is engaged in a broad and expansive regional business community. Winthrop’s beautiful campus encompasses a rich architectural blend of neo-Georgian buildings and is included in the National Register of Historic Places. The attractive recreational and research complex area that surrounds Winthrop Lake is home to Winthrop’s 18 Division I men’s and women’s sports. jobs.description: Provost and Dean of the College Provost and Dean of College Full Time Permanent - Faculty Full Time Permanent - Staff Unclassified View favorites PROVOST AND DEAN OF THE COLLEGE The Citadel, The Military College of South Carolina, seeks an accomplished academic leader to serve as Provost and Dean of the College. Reporting to the President, the Provost serves as the College's Chief Academic Officer, directing the Deans of the College's Schools and collaborating with the Commandant's office to align the academic and military components of a Citadel education. The Provost will also collaborate with the college’s other Vice Presidents as part of the President’s senior leadership team. Founded in 1842, The Citadel is one of the nation's senior military colleges, located on a 300-acre campus in Charleston, South Carolina. The College is home to the South Carolina Corps of Cadets, numbering approximately 2,300 students, as well as The Citadel Graduate College, which serves close to 1,000 students through evening, online, and graduate programs. The Citadel has been named the No. 1 public regional university in the South by U.S. News & World Report for 15 consecutive years, and the No. 1 public college for veterans in the South for eight years. Gen. Frank McKenzie, a 1979 Citadel graduate, began his tenure as the College's 21st President in July of this year. Academic programs are organized across the Tommy and Victoria Baker School of Business, the School of Engineering, the School of Humanities and Social Sciences, the Swain Family School of Science and Mathematics, the Zucker Family School of Education, and the Krause School for Leadership and Ethics, along with The Citadel Graduate College. The College maintains an 11:1 student-to-faculty ratio, and nearly all faculty hold a doctorate or the highest degree in their field. The successful candidate will bring a record of academic leadership, including experience with faculty affairs, curriculum, and accreditation, along with the ability to lead within a structured, values-driven military campus culture. Qualified candidates must hold an earned doctorate or terminal degree, possess scholarly credentials appropriate for a tenured appointment, and demonstrate a successful record of senior academic leadership at the dean level or higher. Experience with both a traditional undergraduate program and adult, graduate, or online education is preferred. Military experience is not necessary, but the Provost will wear a uniform and will hold the grade of Brigadier General in the South Carolina Militia (SCM).
